newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa steps up warnings on Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Dasa steps up warnings on Eurofighter.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) chairman Manfred Bischoff on Sunday stepped up warnings by the firm that any delays in take-up for the four-nation Eurofighter project could cause "quite substantial additional costs."
In an advance release of an interview to appear in Monday's "Die Welt" newspaper, Bischoff said that without orders of a meaningful size for the aircraft, such a project could founder.

The warning is one of a series made to the Bonn government by the Daimler-Benz AG unit, which holds a 30 percent stake in the project. Bonn has said it wants to order 180 of the fighter aircraft but is looking for price cuts.

Bischoff said he understood why cuts in national defence programmes were necessary. "But we also need some understanding for the obligations that we are subject to," he said, referring to the personnel and resource commitments that were required.

Bischoff also spoke in favour of the development by it and other members of the the Airbus consortium of a large-capacity aircraft so as not to leave U.S.-based Boeing Co with a monopoly in that market.

He added that because such a project would cost between 8-10 billion marks it would be necessary to seek other European partners willing to take on "at least 30 percent, if possible 40 percent" of a stake in that specific project.
